title: Localizations of a polynomial ring over a field at maximal ideals have dimension n
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$ an integer, $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\mathfrak M\subset P$ a maximal ideal. Then the localization $P_{\mathfrak M}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] has Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] $\dim(P_{\mathfrak M})=n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), second sentence ('The dimension of k[x_1, ..., x_n]_m is n'); cited for this in the paragraph after Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field, line 35836)

proof.text: (Residue field.) Write $R_i=k[x_1,\dots,x_i]\subseteq P$ for $0\le i\le n$ ($R_0=k$, $R_n=P$) and $\varphi:P\to\kappa=P/\mathfrak M$ for the quotient map; $\kappa$ is a field because $\mathfrak M$ is maximal, and it is a finitely generated $k$-algebra (generated by the images $\alpha_i=\varphi(x_i)$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] $\kappa$ is a finite field extension of $k$; in particular every element of $\kappa$ is algebraic over every subfield containing $k$ (the powers of an element are $k$-linearly dependent). Put $\kappa_0=k$ (its image in $\kappa$) and let $\kappa_i=\kappa_{i-1}(\alpha_i)\subseteq\kappa$ be the smallest subfield containing $\kappa_{i-1}$ and $\alpha_i$, so $\kappa_i=k(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_i)$ and $\kappa_n\supseteq\varphi(P)=\kappa$, i.e. $\kappa_n=\kappa$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), first sentences: 'By the Hilbert Nullstellensatz (Theorem 00FV) we know the residue field kappa = kappa(m) is a finite extension of k ... kappa_i = k(alpha_1, ..., alpha_i)'

proof.text: (The elements $f_i$.) For $1\le i\le n$ let $P_i\in\kappa_{i-1}[T]$ be the monic minimal polynomial of $\alpha_i$ over $\kappa_{i-1}$ (it exists by step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso] (with $F=\kappa_{i-1}$, $\Omega=\kappa$, $\theta=\alpha_i$) $d_i=\deg P_i\ge1$, the map $\kappa_{i-1}[T]\to\kappa$, $T\mapsto\alpha_i$, induces an isomorphism $\kappa_{i-1}[T]/(P_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa_i$, and $\kappa_i=\{g(\alpha_i):g\in\kappa_{i-1}[T]\}$. By induction on $i$ this gives $\kappa_i=k[\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_i]=\varphi(R_i)$ (for $i=0$ trivially; if $\kappa_{i-1}=\varphi(R_{i-1})$, every $g(\alpha_i)$ with $g\in\kappa_{i-1}[T]$ is $\varphi$ of a polynomial in $x_1,\dots,x_i$). So the restriction $\varphi_i=\varphi|_{R_i}:R_i\to\kappa_i$ is surjective. Lift each coefficient of $P_i$ along the surjection $\varphi_{i-1}$, taking $1$ as the lift of the leading coefficient: this gives a monic $Q_i\in R_{i-1}[T]$ of degree $d_i$ whose coefficientwise image is $P_i$. Put $f_i=Q_i(x_i)\in R_i$. Then $\varphi(f_i)=P_i(\alpha_i)=0$, so $f_i\in\mathfrak M\cap R_i$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), 'Note that kappa_i = k[alpha_1, ..., alpha_i] by field theory. Define inductively elements f_i in m cap k[x_1, ..., x_i] ... Set f_i = Q_i(x_i)' (Fields, Lemmas 09G1, 09GN). The source's remark d_1...d_i = [kappa_i : k] (Fields 09HB/09GN) is not used by the argument and is omitted.

proof.text: (Claim: $\ker(\varphi_i)=I_i:=(f_1,\dots,f_i)R_i$ for $0\le i\le n$, i.e. $\varphi_i$ induces an isomorphism $\psi_i:R_i/(f_1,\dots,f_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa_i$.) Induction on $i$. For $i=0$, $\varphi_0:k\to\kappa_0=k$ is the identity and $I_0=0$. Suppose $\ker\varphi_i=I_i$ with $i<n$. Identify $R_{i+1}=R_i[T]$ with $T=x_{i+1}$ (both are polynomial rings over $k$ in $x_1,\dots,x_{i+1}$; the two mutually inverse $k$-algebra maps are given on the variables by the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]). By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel] applied to the surjection $\varphi_i:R_i\to\kappa_i$ (one variable $T$), the coefficient map $c:R_i[T]\to\kappa_i[T]$ is surjective with kernel $I_iR_{i+1}$. Let $e:\kappa_i[T]\to\kappa_{i+1}$ be the surjection $T\mapsto\alpha_{i+1}$, whose kernel is $(P_{i+1})$ by step 2. The composite $e\circ c:R_{i+1}\to\kappa_{i+1}$ agrees with $\varphi_{i+1}$ on $k$ and on $x_1,\dots,x_{i+1}$, hence equals $\varphi_{i+1}$ ([def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], uniqueness in the universal property). Now $\ker\varphi_{i+1}=c^{-1}((P_{i+1}))$. It contains $I_iR_{i+1}=\ker c$ and $f_{i+1}$ (as $c(f_{i+1})=P_{i+1}(T)$). Conversely if $c(g)=hP_{i+1}$, choose $h'\in R_{i+1}$ with $c(h')=h$ (surjectivity of $c$); then $c(g-h'f_{i+1})=0$, so $g\in I_iR_{i+1}+(f_{i+1})=I_{i+1}$. Hence $\ker\varphi_{i+1}=I_{i+1}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), 'We claim that for all i = 0, 1, ..., n there is an isomorphism psi_i : k[x_1, ..., x_i]/(f_1, ..., f_i) = kappa_i ... We prove psi_i is injective by induction ... generated by 1 element over a field and one irreducible equation. By elementary field theory k[x_1, ..., x_{i+1}]/(f_1, ..., f_{i+1}) is a field' (the source's 'elementary field theory' is written out here through the kernel of the coefficient map and the isomorphism kappa_i[T]/(P_{i+1}) = kappa_{i+1})

proof.text: ($\mathfrak M=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ and a chain of primes of length $n$.) For $i=n$, $\varphi_n=\varphi$ and $\ker\varphi=\mathfrak M$, so step 3 gives $\mathfrak M=(f_1,\dots,f_n)P$. For $0\le i\le n$ put $\mathfrak p_i=(f_1,\dots,f_i)P=I_iP$. Identify $P=R_i[x_{i+1},\dots,x_n]$ as in step 3 ([def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]); by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel] applied to the surjection $\varphi_i:R_i\to\kappa_i$ with kernel $I_i$ (step 3) and the variables $x_{i+1},\dots,x_n$, the coefficient map $c_i:P\to\kappa_i[x_{i+1},\dots,x_n]$ is surjective with kernel $I_iP=\mathfrak p_i$, so $P/\mathfrak p_i\cong\kappa_i[x_{i+1},\dots,x_n]$. This is an integral domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain] (a field is a domain), so $\mathfrak p_i$ is a prime ideal. Moreover $\mathfrak p_i\subsetneq\mathfrak p_{i+1}$ for $i<n$: the inclusion is clear, and $c_i(f_{i+1})=P_{i+1}(x_{i+1})$ is a nonzero polynomial (monic of degree $d_{i+1}\ge1$, step 2), so $f_{i+1}\notin\mathfrak p_i$. Hence $(0)=\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n=\mathfrak M$ is a chain of prime ideals of $P$ of length $n$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), 'This implies that m = (f_1, ..., f_n). Moreover ... k[x_1, ..., x_n]/(f_1, ..., f_i) = kappa_i[x_{i+1}, ..., x_n]. Hence (f_1, ..., f_i) is a prime ideal. Thus (0) subset (f_1) subset ... subset (f_1, ..., f_n) = m is a chain of primes of length n' (strictness of the inclusions, left implicit in the source, is shown here)

proof.text: ($\dim P_{\mathfrak M}\ge n$.) The chain of step 4 is a chain of primes of $P$ of length $n$ whose last member $\mathfrak p_n=\mathfrak M$ is contained in $\mathfrak M$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] of $P_{\mathfrak M}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is at least $n$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), last sentence: 'is a chain of primes of length n. The lemma follows.'

proof.text: ($\dim P_{\mathfrak M}\le n$.) A field $k$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $P$, a finite type $k$-algebra, is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and its localization $P_{\mathfrak M}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] (with $S=P\setminus\mathfrak M$). $P_{\mathfrak M}$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak MP_{\mathfrak M}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and by step 4 this ideal is generated by the $n$ elements $f_1/1,\dots,f_n/1$ (an element $a/s$ with $a=\sum g_jf_j\in\mathfrak M$ is $\sum(g_j/s)(f_j/1)$). By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators], $\dim P_{\mathfrak M}\le n$. With step 5, $\dim P_{\mathfrak M}=n$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), first assertion of the lemma ('The ideal m is generated by n elements') together with 'The lemma follows': the upper bound is Algebra, Proposition Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension, line 14521: dim equals the minimal number of generators of an ideal of definition), with Noetherianity from Algebra, Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence)
